lead: Quantum computing / IONQ — the next revolution after AI
smaller: Nuclear power / OKLO — Big Tech wants its own reactors
Rheinmetall / RHM.DE — is European defense the new Magnificent 7?
Dogecoin / DOGE — the meme that pays trivia prizes
why_lead: Quantum has the clearest overlap of price and attention in this day's evidence: IonQ rose 16.68% in the prior session to 21.82 USD on D-Wave's breakthrough headlines, yet it is still down 42.12% over 20 sessions from 37.70, and Stocktwits reported that retail did not budge when IonQ halted its ATM program. Leveraged single-name products and a CNBC 'meme stock' call on Rigetti show the trade is already being packaged for retail, while the institutional debate is about timing rather than direction. The Nvidia Quantum Day headline gives the trade a pending event to test against.
why_smaller: Nuclear power carries the AI-power narrative with a 47.70% 20-session drawdown in Oklo and a Stocktwits headline that retail sentiment pulled back on the surge.
Rheinmetall is the non-AI, non-US trade, with a 73.76% 20-session gain, a 9.62% prior-session move and an eToro headline framing European defense as the new Magnificent 7.
Dogecoin supplies the non-equity trade, with a 32.36% 20-session fall, Robinhood's trivia-prize promotions and the sponsor meme coins' drawdowns as the cautionary tale.
considered_not_chosen: Tesla had the most attention volume in the feed (political coverage, investor surveys and the 'investors want their CEO back' piece), but it is mostly a political and institutional story, so it went into the catalysts and consumer-discretionary block instead of the retail lead.
CoreWeave (CRWV) Stocktwits sentiment and profile pages are dated March 12, but the ticker is absent from the market card, so no price evidence exists and the pages were dropped.
Eutelsat's 650% 'Gamestop effect' surge and its 390% weekly jump are retail-attention stories, but the name is not in the market card, so the trade could not be priced and was left out.

Robinhood and the brokers are an indirect platform exposure to retail flows rather than a retail trade in their own right, so they were not used as a trade; MarketWatch's 'retail traders are getting spooked' item was left out for that reason.
Gold and silver had attention but no move large enough to pass the lead test (gold up 0.48% and silver up 3.89% over 20 sessions), and GameStop and AMC attention pieces were thin.
Adobe's and Dollar General's results were too close to the cutoff, or their dates too uncertain, to use as outcomes, so they were left out of the earnings block.
Polish retail speculation in defense and steel stocks was folded into the Rheinmetall trade and the Poland block rather than taken as a separate trade.
